title: Maximum Calories Burnt from Jumps
summary: Given an integer array heights of size n, where each element heights[i] represents the height of the i^th block in an exercise routine, you start at height 0 (the ground) and must jump onto each block exactly once.
statement: Given an integer array heights of size n, where each element heights[i] represents the height of the i^th block in an exercise routine, you start at height 0 (the ground) and must jump onto each block exactly once. The calories burned for each jump from a block of height a to a block of height b is calculated as (a - b)^2. Additionally, the calories burned for the first jump from the ground to any block is (0 - heights[i])^2. Determine the maximum total calories that can be burned by choosing an optimal sequence of jumps, ensuring no return to the ground after the first jump.
constraints: heights contains one to 100,000 positive block heights.
Start at ground height zero and visit each block exactly once without returning to ground.
A jump from a to b scores (a-b)²; maximize the total.
reference_solution:
def maximum_jump_calories(heights):
    values=sorted(heights);left=0;right=len(values)-1;previous=answer=0
    while left<right:
        answer+=(values[right]-previous)**2;answer+=(values[left]-values[right])**2
        previous=values[left];left+=1;right-=1
    answer+=(values[right]-previous)**2
    return answer

hints: Squared distance rewards repeatedly crossing the widest remaining height gap.
Because ground is below all blocks, visit the current largest height first, then the current smallest, and repeat inward.
Sort heights and use two pointers while tracking the most recently visited low endpoint.
A convex exchange argument moves extremes earlier without decreasing score; alternating remaining extremes realizes every such improving choice.
